name: Cape of Good Hope Route
genZNote: This is the 'okay fine, we'll go the long way' route — slower and more expensive than Suez, but it doesn't depend on any single canal or strait staying open.

sections.heading: 🛳️ Route Path
bullets: European or American Atlantic ports → down the Atlantic Ocean, around South Africa's Cape of Good Hope → into the Indian Ocean → onward to India, Southeast Asia and East Asia.
The historic route used before the Suez Canal opened in 1869, and still the fallback whenever Suez or the Red Sea route is unavailable or too risky.

sections.heading: 📦 Why It Matters
bullets: Adds significant extra distance and time compared with the Suez route, which increases fuel costs and shipping times for goods moving between Europe and Asia.
Becomes commercially important during periods when the Suez Canal or Red Sea route faces disruption, congestion, or security concerns.
Passes major South African ports such as Durban and Cape Town, which benefit economically when more traffic shifts to this route.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Cape of Good Hope route goes around South Africa to connect the Atlantic and Indian Oceans, serving as the historic and current fallback to the Suez Canal.
keyFacts: Path: Atlantic Ocean → around South Africa's Cape of Good Hope → Indian Ocean.
Historic Europe-Asia route before the Suez Canal (1869).
Modern fallback when the Suez/Red Sea route is disrupted.
Longer and more expensive than the Suez route.
commonConfusion: Don't confuse the Cape of Good Hope (Africa, alternative to Suez) with Cape Horn (South America, alternative to Panama) — they solve different route problems.

highYieldFacts: Cape of Good Hope route: fallback to the Suez Canal, goes around Africa.
Longer/costlier but avoids Suez Canal/Red Sea chokepoints entirely.
Was the standard Europe-Asia route before 1869.
commonTraps: Africa's Cape of Good Hope ≠ South America's Cape Horn — same 'go around the continent' idea, two different oceans and two different canals being avoided.
mustRemember: Cape of Good Hope route = the long way around Africa, used when Suez isn't an option.
